Conditions, boundaries and sorting

Unit 2 · Week 4 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open a working copy of sql-starter.sqlite in a school-approved SQLite-capable application and locate its SQL editor. Alternatively execute sql-setup.sql once in a new empty database. Run one SELECT at a time. Use sql-workbook.md, sql-answers.md, sql-worked-queries.sql and sql-expected-results.json. The data are fictional. DueDate is valid YYYY-MM-DD TEXT and Returned is INTEGER 0/1 in this SQLite starter. Fixed reporting date: 8 April 2026. Teacher notes and answers are public.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Conditions, boundaries and sorting

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Return to the earlier single-item Loan model. The reservation model was a separate normalisation exercise. This week uses SELECT queries to read data. Activities are ungraded. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

2. The overdue rule

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and prediction

No under the stated strict-before rule. L002 is active but due exactly on the reporting date. L005 has an older due date but was returned. The fixed date is independent of the actual classroom date. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

3. An overdue query

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

Expect L001 B001 2026-04-06 and L006 B004 2026-04-07. In the supplied valid, fixed-format date text, chronological and text ordering align. TEXT alone does not validate calendar dates. Replacing AND with OR would include returned older loans and active loans due later. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

4. Boundary and return checks

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with predictions

All dates are in 2026. Model the two comparisons separately. AND requires both. If the requirement changed to include due-today loans, <= would add L002. It would not add returned L005. State the boundary rather than guessing from the word overdue. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

5. Grouping borrower alternatives

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

The result is L001 and L002. Without the parentheses, AND has higher precedence than OR and returned B002 loan L005 also qualifies. Trace L005 to show the difference. Parentheses express the intended grouping. OR means either alternative may hold, including both. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

6. Newest due date first

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Use workbook questions 3, 5, 8 and 10 as selected practice. Query: SELECT LoanID, DueDate FROM Loan WHERE Returned = 0 ORDER BY DueDate DESC, LoanID ASC; expected L004, L002, L006, L001. To study a genuine tie, use all loans: L003 and L006 share 7 April, and ascending LoanID places L003 first. Without ORDER BY, no particular row order is guaranteed. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

7. A tie needs another field

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

No. Equal values remain tied on that sort key. Adding unique LoanID ASC decides L003 then L006 for that date. Sorting every field DESC is not required: the primary and tie-break directions can differ. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.

8. A changed boundary

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

L002 now qualifies because its date equals 8 April. L005 remains excluded by Returned = 0. A boundary change affects the rule, not the stored rows. Ask students to justify the result from the two conditions separately. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#sql-basics.
